title: Reverse-time drift and probability-flow drift
goal:
For the VP-SDE the forward drift is $f(x, t) = -\tfrac12\beta(t)\,x$ and the diffusion coefficient is $g(t) = \sqrt{\beta(t)}$.

`gaussian_score(x, t, m0, s0)` returns $\nabla_x \log p_t(x)$ when the data are $x(0) \sim \mathcal{N}(m_0, s_0^2)$. Under the VP-SDE, $p_t$ is Gaussian with mean $m(t)\,m_0$ and variance $m(t)^2 s_0^2 + \sigma^2(t)$, where $m(t)$ and $\sigma^2(t)$ are the kernel quantities from Appendix B, Equation 33.

`reverse_sde_drift(x, t, score)` returns the drift of the reverse-time SDE, $f(x, t) - g(t)^2\,\nabla_x \log p_t(x)$ (Section 3.2, Equation 6).

`pf_ode_drift(x, t, score)` returns the drift of the probability-flow ODE, $f(x, t) - \tfrac12 g(t)^2\,\nabla_x \log p_t(x)$ (Section 4.3, Equation 13).

In the last two functions `score` is the value of $\nabla_x \log p_t(x)$ at `x`, as an array shaped like `x`.
hints: The score of $\mathcal{N}(\mu, v)$ is $-(x - \mu)/v$. Here $\mu = m(t)\,m_0$ and $v = m(t)^2 s_0^2 + 1 - m(t)^2$.
The two drifts differ only in the coefficient on the score term: $g^2$ for the SDE and $\tfrac12 g^2$ for the ODE. The ODE has no noise term to share the work.
If you want to see why the half is right, run the finite-difference test in `tests.py` by hand: it checks that $\partial_t p_t = -\partial_x[\,\text{drift}\cdot p_t\,]$ for your ODE drift.
